turns.text:
# 6-Week Reminder Calendar

I'm building this assuming **Week 1 starts the Monday you begin acting on the plan** — adjust all dates by plugging in your actual start Monday. I'll use "Week X, Day" format so you can drop them into Google Calendar on real dates. Each entry follows a copy-paste-friendly format.

---

## WEEK 1 (10 weeks out)

**Monday**
Title: [J] Send lease termination notice
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Write and deliver written notice to landlord. Photograph or scan the signed notice. Confirm required notice period. Keep a copy in the Move folder.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM, morning of at 8 AM

**Monday**
Title: [J] Start mover/DIY quotes
Time: 10:00 AM
Description: Request 3–4 binding estimates from licensed interstate movers (verify USDOT numbers at safer.fmcsa.dot.gov). Also price U-Haul, Penske, and PODS for comparison. Save all quotes in one spreadsheet.
Reminder: Morning of at 8 AM

**Tuesday**
Title: [M] Research Oregon rentals and neighborhoods
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Spend 1–2 hours browsing listings. Note pet policies, deposits, and commute times. Save top 5 options. Share with partner by end of week.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

**Wednesday**
Title: [M] Schedule car maintenance check
Time: 12:00 PM
Description: Oil, tires, brakes, battery, fluids, belts. Mention you're driving cross-country. Book for this week or next.
Reminder: Morning of at 9 AM

**Thursday**
Title: [M] Book vet visit for dog
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Request full checkup, copy of all vaccine records, rabies certificate, medication refills. Ask about travel anxiety medication. Bring microchip number.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM

**Friday**
Title: [J] Build the move budget
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Use the budget table from the master checklist. Enter real numbers as quotes come in. Agree on a total ceiling and contingency fund. Open a separate "Move" account if helpful.
Reminder: 1 hour before

**Saturday**
Title: [J] Vehicle decision — drive, ship, or fly
Time: 10:00 AM
Description: Get 2–3 vehicle shipping quotes if considering shipping. Compare cost of driving (fuel, lodging, wear) vs. shipping ($900–$1,400 open). Decide today and book if shipping.
Reminder: Morning of at 8 AM

---

## WEEK 2 (9 weeks out)

**Monday**
Title: [J] Compare mover quotes and decide
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Review all estimates side by side. Check valuation coverage options. Choose mover or DIY. Book today — popular dates fill fast.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM, morning of at 8 AM

**Tuesday**
Title: [M] Plan driving route and book dog-friendly lodging
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Map Ohio to Oregon with 2–3 overnight stops. Use BringFido.com or filter for pet-friendly hotels. Book refundable rooms. Save confirmation numbers.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

**Wednesday**
Title: [P] Confirm employer relocation support
Time: 10:00 AM
Description: Ask HR about relocation reimbursement, remote-work approval, start date flexibility, and any paperwork they need. Save any written offer.
Reminder: Morning of at 9 AM

**Thursday**
Title: [J] Gather important documents
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Collect into one folder: IDs, passports, vehicle titles, insurance cards, birth certificates, Social Security cards, tax returns (2 yrs), medical records, prescriptions, dog records. Scan everything to cloud backup.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

**Saturday**
Title: [J] Start garage and storage declutter
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Sort into Keep, Sell, Donate, Trash. Set up an online marketplace listing for big items. Schedule a donation pickup for next week. Less stuff = lower moving cost.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM

---

## WEEK 3 (8 weeks out)

**Monday**
Title: [J] Sign Oregon lease or confirm housing
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Get lease copy, confirm move-in date, pet deposit, and key pickup. Save lease in Move folder. If not ready, book 1–2 weeks of temporary housing (dog-friendly Airbnb or extended-stay).
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM

**Monday**
Title: [M] Schedule Oregon internet installation
Time: 10:00 AM
Description: Internet installs can be backlogged 2+ weeks. Call the provider now and schedule for move-in day or the day before if possible.
Reminder: Morning of at 9 AM

**Wednesday**
Title: [M] Map Oregon utilities and set up accounts
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Identify electric, gas, water, sewer, and trash providers at the new address. Create accounts online. Schedule start dates for move-in day.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

**Friday**
Title: [J] Order packing supplies
Time: 12:00 PM
Description: Boxes (small, medium, large, wardrobe), packing tape and dispenser, bubble wrap, packing paper, markers, mattress bags, furniture pads. Ask local stores for free boxes too.
Reminder: Morning of at 9 AM

**Saturday**
Title: [J] Declutter round 2 — closets and guest room
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Apply the rule: if you haven't used it in a year and it's not sentimental, let it go. List sellable items. Bag donations.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM

---

## WEEK 4 (7 weeks out)

**Monday**
Title: [M] Confirm mover or truck booking in writing
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Get written confirmation of date, time, crew size, valuation coverage, and total cost. Save to Move folder. Note cancellation policy.
Reminder: Morning of at 8 AM

**Wednesday**
Title: [M] If shipping car — book the carrier
Time: 10:00 AM
Description: Confirm pickup window, delivery window, open vs. enclosed, payment terms, and insurance coverage. Save contract.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM

**Thursday**
Title: [M] Find an Oregon vet and emergency vet
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Research vets near the new address. Read reviews. Call to confirm they're accepting new patients. Ask about records transfer. Save the nearest 24-hour emergency vet number in your phone.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

**Saturday**
Title: [J] Begin packing non-essential rooms
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Start with guest room, storage areas, books, decor, out-of-season clothes. Label every box with room, contents, and priority (open first / open later). Pack heavy items in small boxes.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM

---

## WEEK 5 (6 weeks out — 1 month to move)

**Monday**
Title: [J] File USPS change of address
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Go to usps.com/move. Set the forwarding start date for 2–3 days before move-in. Costs $1.10 to verify identity. Save confirmation number.
Reminder: Morning of at 8 AM

**Monday**
Title: [J] Schedule Ohio utility shutoffs
Time: 10:00 AM
Description: Call electric, gas, water, sewer, trash, internet, and cable. Set disconnect for the day after you leave. Request final bills sent to your new address. Save confirmation numbers.
Reminder: Morning of at 9 AM

**Tuesday**
Title: [J] Notify banks, insurance, and subscriptions of address change
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Update address with: banks, credit cards, auto insurance, health insurance, renter's/homeowner's insurance, employer payroll, student loans, subscriptions (streaming, deliveries, memberships). Keep a checklist and check each one off.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

**Wednesday**
Title: [M] Check Ohio vehicle title and lien status
Time: 12:00 PM
Description: Confirm you have a clean title. If there's a lien, call the lender about releasing or transferring it. You need the title to register in Oregon.
Reminder: Morning of at 9 AM

**Thursday**
Title: [M] Research Oregon DMV requirements
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: New residents have a limited window to get an Oregon license and registration. Check what documents you need (ID, proof of residency, title, insurance, emissions). Save the nearest Oregon DMV location and hours.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

**Saturday**
Title: [J] Pack kitchen non-essentials and dining room
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Pack specialty appliances, extra dishes, serving ware, cookbooks, table linens. Keep one pot, one pan, one plate and bowl per person, one set of utensils, and a coffee setup for the last week.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM

---

## WEEK 6 (5 weeks out — 4 weeks to move)

**Monday**
Title: [J] Cancel or transfer local services
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Gym memberships, library cards, dry cleaning, house cleaning, lawn care, pest control, security system. Cancel or transfer each one. Save confirmation emails.
Reminder: Morning of at 8 AM

**Tuesday**
Title: [M] Order dog travel supplies
Time: 12:00 PM
Description: Car crate or barrier, travel water bowl, poop bags for the road, calming treats or spray, familiar blanket, extra leash. If the vet prescribed anti-anxiety meds, fill the prescription now.
Reminder: Morning of at 9 AM

**Wednesday**
Title: [J] Pack bedrooms except daily essentials
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Off-season clothes, extra bedding, decor, books. Leave out 1 week of clothes per person, one set of sheets, pillows, and towels. Put mattress bags aside for moving day.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

**Saturday**
Title: [J] Pack living room and remaining common areas
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Electronics (photograph cable setups first), art, lamps, rugs, shelves. Label fragile items clearly. Keep one entertainment setup for the last few days if you want.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM

---

## WEEK 7 (4 weeks out — 3 weeks to move)

**Monday**
Title: [J] Pack bathroom non-essentials
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Extra towels, cleaning supplies, medicine cabinet overflow. Keep a toiletry bag per person with a week's worth of essentials.
Reminder: Morning of at 8 AM

**Tuesday**
Title: [J] Sell or donate remaining unwanted items
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Final push. Drop off donations, ship sold items, put remaining giveaways on the curb or in a free group. Schedule bulk trash pickup if needed.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

**Wednesday**
Title: [M] Confirm car shipping pickup date and details
Time: 10:00 AM
Description: Reconfirm with the carrier: pickup date, location, your contact number, and payment method. Remove personal items from the car. Take photos of the car's condition before handoff.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM

**Friday**
Title: [M] Update dog's ID tag
Time: 12:00 PM
Description: Order or make a temporary tag with your cell number and new city. Attach it before you leave. Set a reminder to update the microchip registry after arrival.
Reminder: Morning of at 9 AM

**Saturday**
Title: [J] Pack "Last Out, First In" boxes — one per room
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: These are the first boxes you open. Kitchen: paper plates, utensils, coffee, snacks, dish soap, paper towels. Bedroom: sheets, pillows, towels, phone chargers. Bathroom: toilet paper, soap, shampoo, toothbrushes. Mark them with bright tape.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM

---

## WEEK 8 (3 weeks out — 2 weeks to move)

**Monday**
Title: [J] Confirm mover arrival window and payment
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Call or email to reconfirm date, time, address, elevator or parking needs, and payment method. Get the final written estimate. Print the Bill of Lading if available.
Reminder: Morning of at 8 AM

**Tuesday**
Title: [M] Confirm Oregon utility start dates
Time: 10:00 AM
Description: Call or check online for electric, gas, water, internet. Confirm everything is active on move-in day.
Reminder: Morning of at 9 AM

**Wednesday**
Title: [M] Auto insurance — confirm Oregon coverage
Time: 12:00 PM
Description: Call your insurer. Confirm your policy covers you in Oregon from move-in day. Ask about updating the policy to Oregon rates and requirements. Get a new insurance card if needed.
Reminder: Morning of at 9 AM

**Friday**
Title: [J] Pack final non-essentials
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Everything except daily-use items should be boxed. Begin cleaning behind packed areas.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

---

## WEEK 9 (2 weeks out — 1 week to move)

**Monday**
Title: [J] Defrost freezer and clean fridge
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Unplug the freezer. Use up or donate perishable food. Clean both appliances. Leave doors open to dry.
Reminder: Day before at 7 PM

**Tuesday**
Title: [J] Photo inventory of valuables
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Take photos of furniture, electronics, and anything valuable. Note serial numbers. Save photos to cloud and a USB drive you carry with you.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

**Wednesday**
Title: [M] Pack the dog's travel kit
Time: 12:00 PM
Description: Food (enough for travel + 3 days), bowls, leash, harness, poop bags, medications, calming aids, vet records copy, blanket, favorite toy, crate or car barrier, paper towels for accidents.
Reminder: Morning of at 9 AM

**Thursday**
Title: [J] Pack the car essentials box
Time: 7:00 PM
Description: Use the Moving Day Essentials one-pager. Pack everything listed into one box or bag that stays in the car.
Reminder: 30 minutes before

**Friday**
Title: [J] Final clean and walk-through prep
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Clean the apartment or house. Take photos of every room, closets, appliances, and exterior. These protect your deposit.
Reminder: Morning of at 8 AM

---

## WEEK 10 — MOVING DAY WEEK

**Day before move**
Title: [J] Final walk-through and prep
Time: 6:00 PM
Description: Confirm everything is packed except the car essentials box, bed linens for tonight, and toiletries. Set alarms for tomorrow. Confirm mover arrival time. Lay out clothes for tomorrow. Charge all devices. Fill the gas tank.
Reminder: 2 PM

**Moving day**
Title: [J] MOVING DAY
Time: 7:00 AM
Description: See the Moving Day Essentials one-pager. Walk-through photos. Meet movers. Read and sign Bill of Lading. Return keys and get receipt. Final meter read photos. Load the dog last. Start driving.
Reminder: 6:00 AM

**Day after arrival**
Title: [J] Move-in photos and damage check
Time: 9:00 AM
Description: Photograph every room, closet, appliance, and any existing damage. Send the photos and a written note to the landlord within 24–48 hours or per lease terms.
Reminder: Morning of at 8 AM

# MOVING DAY ESSENTIALS

**Keep this page in the car. Do not load any of this onto the truck.**

## Documents — in one folder or pouch [J]

- [ ] Driver's licenses and passports
- [ ] Vehicle titles, registrations, insurance cards
- [ ] Moving contract, estimate, and Bill of Lading
- [ ] Vehicle shipping receipt and carrier contact info
- [ ] Ohio lease (move-out) and Oregon lease (move-in)
- [ ] Dog: rabies certificate, vaccine records, microchip number, vet contact
- [ ] Medical prescriptions (current, for all household members)
- [ ] Birth certificates, Social Security cards, marriage certificate
- [ ] Insurance policy numbers (auto, renters, health)
- [ ] New landlord name, phone, lockbox code or key pickup instructions
- [ ] Emergency contacts list (printed, not just on phone)

## Overnight bags — one per person [M and P each pack their own]

- [ ] 3 days of clothes, pajamas, underwear, socks
- [ ] Toiletries (toothbrush, toothpaste, deodorant, shampoo, soap, contacts, glasses)
- [ ] Medications (daily prescriptions, pain reliever, allergy meds)
- [ ] Phone charger, laptop, laptop charger
- [ ] Earbuds or headphones
- [ ] One towel each

## Dog travel kit [M]

- [ ] Food (enough for travel days plus 3 extra days)
- [ ] Portable water and food bowls
- [ ] Leash, harness, collar with updated ID tag
- [ ] Poop bags
- [ ] Medications and calming aids
- [ ] Favorite blanket or bed
- [ ] Favorite toy
- [ ] Paper towels and plastic bags for accidents
- [ ] Crate or car barrier (secured before departure)

## Car survival kit [M]

- [ ] Water bottles (for people and dog)
- [ ] Snacks and road food
- [ ] First aid kit
- [ ] Flashlight and batteries
- [ ] Jumper cables or portable jump starter
- [ ] Phone car charger and backup battery
- [ ] Paper maps or printed directions (in case of dead phone)
- [ ] Tire pressure gauge
- [ ] Blanket
- [ ] Umbrella or rain jackets
- [ ] Cash ($200+ in small bills for tolls, tips, emergencies)
- [ ] Sunglasses

## Cleaning and move-out kit [P]

- [ ] All-purpose cleaner spray
- [ ] Paper towels or rags
- [ ] Broom and dustpan (or leave for donation after final sweep)
- [ ] Trash bags (3–5 large)
- [ ] Keys, garage remotes, fobs (to return to landlord)

## First-night box — open immediately at the new place [J]

- [ ] Toilet paper
- [ ] Hand soap
- [ ] Paper plates, cups, plastic utensils
- [ ] One sharp knife and a can opener
- [ ] Coffee, tea, sugar, creamer (and the coffee maker if you need it to function)
- [ ] Dish soap and a sponge
- [ ] Sheets and pillowcases for one bed
- [ ] Pillows (carry in car, not in box)
- [ ] Phone chargers (duplicates if possible)
- [ ] A few hangers
- [ ] Light bulbs (in case the new place has empty sockets)
- [ ] Basic toolkit: screwdriver, pliers, box cutter, tape

## Moving day morning sequence [J unless noted]

1. Walk the dog and feed early [M]
2. Strip beds, pack final toiletries and sheets into overnight bags
3. Do a final walk-through — photograph every room, closets, and exterior
4. Meet movers — read the Bill of Lading and inventory before signing
5. Watch for damage notes on the inventory — add your own if needed
6. Confirm delivery address and your phone number with the crew lead
7. Take final meter readings and photograph them
8. Return keys and remotes to landlord — get a written or text receipt
9. Secure the dog in the car with crate or barrier, water, and a familiar blanket [M]
10. Final check: documents folder, overnight bags, dog kit, car kit, first-night box all in the car
11. Drive safe — stop every 2–3 hours for the dog — keep the car cool — never leave the dog in a parked car

turns.text:
# Room-by-Room Packing Checklist

## Labeling System

Before you pack a single box, grab a thick marker and use this format on the top and at least one side of every box:

**ROOM — Contents — Priority — Fragile?**

Example: **KITCHEN — Coffee maker, mugs, spices — OPEN FIRST — FRAGILE**

Use three priority levels: **OPEN FIRST** (things you need within hours of arrival), **OPEN SOON** (within the first few days), and **OPEN LATER** (seasonal, decorative, rarely used). If you want to go further, number each box and keep a running list in your phone's notes app — "Kitchen #4: blender, mixing bowls, baking sheets" — so you can find anything without opening every box.

Color-coding with colored tape or stickers works well too. Pick one color per room and slap it on. The movers or your future selves will thank you.

---

## Fragile-Packing Rules (apply everywhere)

These apply to every room, so internalize them before you start.

Dishes, glasses, and ceramics go on their edges (not flat) inside cells or wrapped individually in packing paper. Never use newspaper directly on anything you eat from — the ink transfers. Nest bowls with paper between each one. Fill every gap in the box with crumpled paper or towels so nothing shifts. If you can shake the box and hear movement, add more fill.

Mirrors, frames, and glass art get an X of painter's tape across the glass (limits shatter spread), then get wrapped in bubble wrap and placed in a flat mirror box or between two pieces of cardboard taped together. Mark FRAGILE and THIS SIDE UP.

Electronics get wrapped in anti-static bubble wrap if you have it, or soft cloths. If you saved the original box, use it. Photograph the cable setup behind TVs and entertainment centers before unplugging. Put all cords and remotes in a labeled zip-lock bag taped to the device or its box.

Lamps get disassembled: remove the shade, wrap it in a large garbage bag to keep it clean, and pack it upright in a tall box with paper around it. Wrap the base separately.

Liquids always get a strip of plastic wrap under the cap, then cap tightened, then placed upright in a zip-lock bag inside the box. Pack liquids in small boxes so weight stays manageable and leaks stay contained.

---

## Kitchen

**Responsibility:** J
**Estimated time:** 4–6 hours total (split across 2 sessions)
**Priority:** Pack non-essentials 3–4 weeks out. Pack daily-use items last, the day before or morning of the move.
**Suggested boxes:** 8–15 medium, 3–5 small (for heavy items like cans and ceramics), 1–2 large (for lightweight bulky items like plastic containers)

**Non-essentials (pack first, OPEN LATER or OPEN SOON):**

- [ ] Specialty appliances: stand mixer, food processor, blender, waffle maker, slow cooker, instant pot, bread maker
- [ ] Baking supplies: cake pans, muffin tins, cookie sheets, rolling pin, decorating tools
- [ ] Serving ware: platters, punch bowls, gravy boats, holiday dishes, entertaining pieces
- [ ] Extra dish sets and glassware beyond daily use
- [ ] Cookbooks and recipe binders
- [ ] Table linens: tablecloths, cloth napkins, placemats
- [ ] Wine and bar supplies: bottles (wrap individually, pack upright in small boxes), cocktail tools, bar glasses
- [ ] Vases, decorative bowls, and countertop decor
- [ ] Rarely used utensils and gadgets: melon baller, mandoline, spiralizer, fondue set

**Daily essentials (pack last, OPEN FIRST):**

- [ ] One pot, one pan, one baking sheet
- [ ] One plate, one bowl, one mug per person
- [ ] One set of utensils per person plus one sharp knife
- [ ] Can opener, bottle opener, corkscrew
- [ ] Coffee maker or French press, coffee, filters, sugar, creamer
- [ ] Dish soap, one sponge, one dish towel
- [ ] Paper towels, paper plates, and plastic utensils for moving day and the first night
- [ ] Trash bags
- [ ] Snacks and water bottles for the road

**Declutter tips:** Open every drawer and cabinet. If you have duplicate whisks, three sets of measuring cups, or a panini press you used once in 2019, let it go. Spices expire — check dates and toss anything older than 2–3 years. Mismatched food storage containers without lids go in recycling. Chipped or cracked dishes get tossed. Donate usable items to a local kitchen supply thrift shop or community kitchen.

---

## Living Room

**Responsibility:** J
**Estimated time:** 3–4 hours
**Priority:** Pack 2–3 weeks out, keeping one entertainment setup for the final days if you want.
**Suggested boxes:** 4–8 medium, 2–3 small (for heavy books or media), 1–2 large (for throw pillows, blankets, lampshades), specialty boxes for TV or mirrors if applicable

**Items:**

- [ ] Books: pack in small boxes, spine-down, fill gaps with packing paper. These get heavy fast — never fill a large box with only books
- [ ] DVDs, games, vinyl records: small boxes, upright like files
- [ ] TV: original box if you have it, otherwise wrap in a moving blanket and use a TV box. Photograph cable setup first. Put remote in a labeled zip-lock bag
- [ ] Sound system, speakers, streaming devices: wrap each piece, label cords
- [ ] Gaming consoles and controllers: wrap individually, keep cords bundled and labeled
- [ ] Decorative items: picture frames (see fragile rules), candles, figurines, sculptures, vases
- [ ] Lamps: disassemble, pack shades separately upright, wrap bases
- [ ] Throw pillows, blankets, curtains: use these as padding inside boxes or pack in large trash bags (not for trash — label them clearly)
- [ ] Rugs: roll tightly, secure with twine or stretch wrap, stand upright in the truck
- [ ] Shelving and small furniture: disassemble if possible, bag hardware in a zip-lock taped to the piece, wrap corners in bubble wrap
- [ ] Coffee table books, magazines, coasters
- [ ] Remotes and batteries: one labeled zip-lock bag for all remotes

**Declutter tips:** Books are one of the heaviest things to move per cubic foot. Be ruthless. If you won't reread it, donate it. Same goes for DVDs and CDs in a streaming era. Old magazines, catalogs, and dead remotes go. If you have decorative items you've been displaying out of obligation rather than love, this is the moment to pass them on.

---

## Primary Bedroom

**Responsibility:** P
**Estimated time:** 2–3 hours
**Priority:** Pack non-essentials 2–3 weeks out. Pack daily clothes and bedding the morning of the move.
**Suggested boxes:** 4–8 medium, 1–2 wardrobe boxes (if you have hanging clothes worth protecting), 2–3 large (for bedding and pillows if not using bags)

**Non-essentials (pack first):**

- [ ] Off-season clothing: winter coats in summer, etc.
- [ ] Shoes beyond daily wear: wrap each pair in packing paper or keep in shoe boxes
- [ ] Extra bedding sets, quilts, and decorative pillows
- [ ] Jewelry: carry valuable jewelry with you in the car, not on the truck. Use a small zip-lock or jewelry roll
- [ ] Dresser contents: you can leave clothes in dresser drawers if the movers allow it and the dresser is light enough — ask. Otherwise, pack drawer contents into bags and label by drawer
- [ ] Nightstand contents: books, journals, chargers, personal items
- [ ] Under-bed storage items
- [ ] Wall art, mirrors, and photos (see fragile rules)
- [ ] Hamper, iron, ironing board, hangers (bundle hangers with a rubber band)

**Daily essentials (pack last, OPEN FIRST):**

- [ ] 3 days of clothes, underwear, socks (into overnight bag for the car)
- [ ] Pajamas
- [ ] Shoes you'll wear during the move and drive
- [ ] Phone charger and bedside essentials
- [ ] One set of sheets, one set of pillowcases, pillows — carry pillows in the car
- [ ] Alarm clock or confirm phone alarm is set

**Declutter tips:** Try everything on. If it doesn't fit, you don't love it, or you haven't worn it in a year, donate it. Worn-out socks and underwear get tossed, not donated. Old pillows that have lost their shape get replaced — they're cheap and not worth shipping 2,400 miles. This is the single best room for reducing box count because clothing and bedding are bulky.

---

## Guest Room / Spare Room

**Responsibility:** M
**Estimated time:** 1–2 hours
**Priority:** Pack first — 4+ weeks out. This room usually has the least essential items.
**Suggested boxes:** 2–5 medium, 1 large

**Items:**

- [ ] Guest bedding and pillows
- [ ] Extra towels stored here
- [ ] Hobby supplies and craft materials
- [ ] Exercise equipment: disassemble if needed, wipe down
- [ ] Stored luggage: use suitcases as packing containers for soft items — this saves box count
- [ ] Board games, puzzles, card games
- [ ] Gift wrapping supplies
- [ ] Seasonal decorations (holiday items)
- [ ] Anything in the closet that's been in there since the last move

**Declutter tips:** This room is typically the declutter gold mine. If you stored it here because you didn't know where else to put it, ask yourself whether you actually need it in Oregon. Holiday decorations can be trimmed to favorites only. Broken exercise equipment, dusty craft projects you'll never finish, and guest bedding for a guest room you might not have — all fair game.

---

## Bathroom(s)

**Responsibility:** P
**Estimated time:** 1–2 hours per bathroom
**Priority:** Pack non-essentials 2 weeks out. Pack daily toiletries the morning of the move.
**Suggested boxes:** 1–3 small (liquids are heavy), 1 medium

**Non-essentials (pack first):**

- [ ] Extra towels and washcloths beyond one set per person
- [ ] Backup toiletries and bulk supplies
- [ ] Hair tools: straightener, curling iron, dryer (wrap cords, let cool completely before packing)
- [ ] Medicine cabinet overflow: first aid supplies, bandages, cold medicine, vitamins
- [ ] Cleaning supplies under the sink: seal all lids with plastic wrap, pack upright in a small box lined with a trash bag
- [ ] Bathroom decor: shower curtain (wash first or replace at destination), bath mat, wastebasket
- [ ] Rarely used items: nail kits, face masks, travel-size bottles

**Daily essentials (pack morning of, OPEN FIRST):**

- [ ] Toothbrushes, toothpaste, floss
- [ ] Deodorant, soap, shampoo, conditioner
- [ ] Contact lenses, solution, glasses
- [ ] Daily medications and prescriptions
- [ ] Razor
- [ ] One towel per person
- [ ] Toilet paper (at least 2 rolls for the first night at the new place)
- [ ] Hand soap

**Declutter tips:** Check expiration dates on every medication, sunscreen, and product. Most people have a bathroom cabinet full of expired items. Travel-size bottles from hotels you'll never use, old makeup, dried-out nail polish, and that half-used bottle of something you didn't like all get tossed. Consolidate duplicate products.

---

## Home Office / Desk Area

**Responsibility:** M
**Estimated time:** 2–3 hours
**Priority:** Pack non-essentials 2–3 weeks out. Keep your computer and work setup running until the last possible day.
**Suggested boxes:** 3–5 medium, 2 small (for heavy files and supplies)

**Non-essentials (pack first):**

- [ ] Books and reference materials
- [ ] File cabinet contents: sort, shred anything you don't need, keep 2–3 years of tax records and anything you can't replace
- [ ] Office supplies: staplers, tape, pens, paper (be honest about how many pens you actually need)
- [ ] Printers, scanners, shredders: original boxes if available, otherwise wrap well and pack cords in labeled bags
- [ ] Extra cables, adapters, and chargers: label every one with what it goes to
- [ ] Desk accessories and decor

**Daily essentials (pack last):**

- [ ] Laptop and charger — this goes in the car, not on the truck
- [ ] External hard drives and USB drives with backups — car, not truck
- [ ] Webcam, headset, and anything needed for remote work
- [ ] A notepad and pen for moving-day notes and phone numbers

**Declutter tips:** Shred old bank statements, expired warranties, old manuals (most are online now), and junk mail that piled up. Recycle dead pens. Old tech — the drawer full of phone cases for phones you no longer own, ancient chargers, broken headphones — recycle it through an e-waste program, don't move it.

---

## Garage / Storage / Utility Areas

**Responsibility:** J
**Estimated time:** 3–5 hours
**Priority:** Pack first — 4+ weeks out. This is where the biggest declutter gains happen.
**Suggested boxes:** Varies widely — 3–10 boxes plus loose items. Use original packaging for power tools when possible.

**Items:**

- [ ] Tools: consolidate into a toolbox or tool bag. Wrap sharp edges in cardboard and tape
- [ ] Garden tools and outdoor furniture: clean soil off everything. Drain fuel from gas-powered equipment — movers won't transport fuel or propane
- [ ] Holiday and seasonal decorations
- [ ] Sporting equipment: bikes, skis, camping gear
- [ ] Automotive supplies: drain or dispose of fluids. Movers won't take flammable or hazardous items (oil, paint, gasoline, propane, pesticides, pool chemicals). Check your mover's prohibited items list
- [ ] Luggage and storage bins
- [ ] Paint cans: unless you need them for touch-up at the new place, leave them. Take a photo of the label for color-matching later
- [ ] Ladders, shelving units: disassemble, bag hardware
- [ ] Laundry supplies: partially used detergent and bleach are often not worth moving. Seal anything you do bring

**Declutter tips:** This is the room where people move things they never use from house to house for decades. Broken items waiting to be fixed, duplicate tools, old paint, mystery hardware, and furniture stored "just in case" should all be evaluated hard. If you haven't touched it in 2+ years, let it go. Dispose of hazardous materials at a local collection event or drop-off — don't put them in the trash.

---

## Dining Room

**Responsibility:** P
**Estimated time:** 1–2 hours
**Priority:** Pack 2–3 weeks out.
**Suggested boxes:** 2–5 medium, 1–2 small for heavy items like china

**Items:**

- [ ] China, fine glassware, crystal: individually wrap each piece, pack on edge, fill all gaps, mark FRAGILE
- [ ] Serving dishes, platters, centerpieces
- [ ] Table linens and cloth napkins
- [ ] Candlesticks and candles
- [ ] Buffet or hutch contents: pack contents, then disassemble furniture if needed
- [ ] Chair cushions: stuff into large trash bags, label NOT TRASH
- [ ] Dining table: if it disassembles, bag all hardware in a zip-lock taped to the underside

**Declutter tips:** Formal dining sets that only come out at holidays are heavy and expensive to move. If you use them and love them, pack carefully and move them. If you've inherited a set out of obligation and never use it, this may be the time to pass it on to a family member or consign it.

---

## Laundry Area

**Responsibility:** P
**Estimated time:** 30–60 minutes
**Priority:** Pack

## Laundry Area (continued)

**Responsibility:** P
**Estimated time:** 30–60 minutes
**Priority:** Pack 1 week out except for one last load of towels and clothes.
**Suggested boxes:** 1–2 medium, 1 small

**Items:**

- [ ] Detergent, fabric softener, stain remover: seal caps with plastic wrap, bag in zip-locks, pack upright in a small box lined with a trash bag
- [ ] Dryer sheets, clothespins, lint roller
- [ ] Iron and ironing board: let the iron cool completely, wrap the cord, collapse the board and wrap in a moving blanket or old sheet
- [ ] Drying rack: collapse and bundle with twine or stretch wrap
- [ ] Laundry baskets and hampers: use these as packing containers for soft items like towels, rags, and cleaning cloths — saves boxes
- [ ] Spare hangers: bundle with rubber bands, put in a trash bag labeled NOT TRASH
- [ ] Sewing kit, stain sticks, mending supplies
- [ ] Cleaning rags and microfiber cloths: keep 2–3 out for move-day cleaning, pack the rest
- [ ] Washer and dryer: if you own them and they're coming with you, disconnect hoses, drain them, and secure the washer drum with transit bolts (check the manual or look up your model — running a washer without transit bolts during transport can destroy the drum). Tape the power cords to the back of each unit. If you don't have transit bolts, most appliance stores sell universal kits for a few dollars

**Declutter tips:** Half-used bottles of detergent and softener are heavy and leak-prone. If a bottle is less than a quarter full, use it up or give it away rather than packing it. Stained or threadbare cleaning rags, single socks from the lost-sock pile, and broken hangers get tossed. If you're leaving the washer and dryer behind, clean them out thoroughly as a courtesy.

---

## Entryway, Mudroom, and Coat Closet

**Responsibility:** M
**Estimated time:** 30–60 minutes
**Priority:** Pack 1–2 weeks out except for daily-use coats and shoes.
**Suggested boxes:** 1–2 medium, 1 large (for coats if not using a wardrobe box)

**Items:**

- [ ] Off-season coats and jackets
- [ ] Hats, scarves, gloves, mittens
- [ ] Umbrellas
- [ ] Shoe rack and shoes beyond daily wear: wrap each pair in packing paper
- [ ] Backpacks, tote bags, reusable shopping bags: stuff these with soft items like scarves and gloves to save space
- [ ] Pet leashes, harnesses, and accessories stored here (keep one leash and harness out for travel)
- [ ] Keys: collect every spare key, label them, and decide what to return and what to keep
- [ ] Mail organizer, entryway tray contents, miscellaneous drawer items
- [ ] Welcome mat: shake out, roll, and secure with twine
- [ ] Wall hooks, mirror, and entryway decor

**Declutter tips:** Count your reusable bags. You probably have thirty. Keep five. Shoes that hurt, single gloves, and broken umbrellas go. If you have a junk drawer in the entryway, dump it out and sort it. Most of it is trash, expired coupons, and mystery keys.

---

## Outdoor and Patio

**Responsibility:** J
**Estimated time:** 1–2 hours
**Priority:** Pack 2–3 weeks out. Clean and dry everything before boxing.
**Suggested boxes:** Mostly loose items and furniture, 1–3 medium boxes for smaller items

**Items:**

- [ ] Patio furniture: clean, dry, disassemble if possible, wrap legs and corners in bubble wrap, bag hardware
- [ ] Grill: clean thoroughly, remove propane tank (movers won't transport it — give it away or leave it), wrap grates
- [ ] Planters and pots: empty soil, clean, nest smaller pots inside larger ones with paper between
- [ ] Garden hose: drain completely, coil and secure with twine
- [ ] Outdoor cushions and pillows: stuff into large trash bags, label NOT TRASH
- [ ] String lights, lanterns, outdoor decor
- [ ] Doormat: shake, roll, and secure
- [ ] Kids' or dog's outdoor toys
- [ ] Gardening gloves, hand tools, watering cans
- [ ] Any stored firewood: leave it behind — transporting firewood across state lines can spread invasive insects and may be restricted or prohibited

**Declutter tips:** Cheap plastic patio furniture often costs less to replace than to ship. Cracked pots, rusted tools, and dead plants stay behind. If you have a grill you don't love, sell it and buy one in Oregon rather than paying to move it.

---

# 10-Week Packing Timeline

This is designed to be printed on one page. Adjust box counts based on your actual household size. These are estimates for a 1–2 bedroom apartment or small house for two people.

---

**WEEKS 1–2: Gather and declutter only. No packing yet.**

Who: J | Est. boxes packed: 0

Sort every room into Keep, Sell, Donate, Trash. Focus on the garage, storage areas, guest room, and closets first. List items for sale online. Schedule donation pickups. Order packing supplies at the end of Week 2.

---

**WEEK 3: Garage, storage, and guest room**

Who: M leads garage/storage, M leads guest room | Est. boxes: 5–12

Pack everything in the garage that's coming with you. Pack the entire guest room. These are your least-used spaces and the easiest place to start. Use suitcases and storage bins as packing containers for soft items.

---

**WEEK 4: Dining room, holiday/seasonal items, and outdoor/patio**

Who: P leads dining room, J leads outdoor | Est. boxes: 5–10

Wrap china and glassware carefully. Pack all seasonal decorations. Clean and pack outdoor furniture and grill. Sell or give away the propane tank.

---

**WEEK 5: Home office, books, and media**

Who: M leads office, J leads books/media | Est. boxes: 5–10

Shred old files. Pack reference books, supplies, and non-essential electronics. Keep your daily work computer and setup running. Pack all DVDs, games, vinyl, and books from every room this week. Books go in small boxes only.

---

**WEEK 6: Living room non-essentials**

Who: J | Est. boxes: 5–10

Pack decor, art, lamps, extra blankets, and throw pillows. Leave one entertainment setup if you want it for the final two weeks. Roll and secure rugs. Photograph cable setups before unplugging anything.

---

**WEEK 7: Kitchen non-essentials and laundry area**

Who: J leads kitchen, P leads laundry | Est. boxes: 6–12

Pack specialty appliances, baking supplies, serving ware, extra dish sets, bar supplies, cookbooks, and table linens. Pack all laundry area items except one load's worth of detergent. Keep daily kitchen essentials out: one pot, one pan, one plate and bowl per person, utensils, coffee maker, and dish soap.

---

**WEEK 8: Bedrooms (non-essentials) and closets**

Who: P leads primary bedroom, M leads closets and entryway | Est. boxes: 6–12

Pack off-season clothes, extra shoes, spare bedding, jewelry (goes in the car), nightstand contents, wall art, and closet overflow. Leave out 3 days of clothes per person, one set of sheets, pillows, and daily shoes. Pack the entryway and coat closet.

---

**WEEK 9: Bathrooms (non-essentials), remaining living room, final kitchen items**

Who: P leads bathrooms, J leads the rest | Est. boxes: 4–8

Pack extra towels, medicine cabinet overflow, cleaning supplies, and hair tools. Pack the last of the living room (remaining electronics, the TV, final decor). Pack remaining kitchen items down to your moving-day essentials. Each person keeps a toiletry bag with daily items. Leave out two rolls of toilet paper, hand soap, and one towel per person.

---

**WEEK 10: Final packing, moving day, and go**

Who: J | Est. boxes: 2–5

Monday through Thursday: Pack the final toiletries, bedding, cleaning supplies, and remaining daily items. Defrost the fridge. Do a final cleaning pass. Pack the OPEN FIRST boxes and the car essentials box. Load overnight bags, dog kit, documents, and car survival kit into the car.

Moving day: Movers or truck gets loaded. Walk-through photos. Return keys. Drive to Oregon.

---

**Estimated total box count: 40–80 boxes**

This varies widely by household. A minimalist couple might use 30. A couple with a full garage, home office, and lots of kitchen gear could hit 80 or more. When in doubt, order 10–15 extra boxes — most suppliers take back unused ones.

---

**Quick box-size guide for reference:**

Small boxes (16×12×12 or similar) are for heavy things: books, canned goods, tools, ceramics, files, and liquids. Medium boxes (18×18×16 or similar) are your workhorse — most items go here. Large boxes (18×18×24 or similar) are only for lightweight bulky items: pillows, lampshades, plastic containers, linens, and stuffed animals. If a large box is heavy enough that you can't comfortably lift it, you've packed it wrong.

# KITCHEN

**Who:** J | **Time:** 4–6 hrs (two sessions) | **Priority:** Non-essentials 3–4 wks out, daily items morning of move
**Boxes:** 8–15 medium, 3–5 small, 1–2 large

- [ ] Specialty appliances (stand mixer, blender, slow cooker, food processor)
- [ ] Baking pans, muffin tins, cookie sheets, rolling pin
- [ ] Serving ware, platters, holiday dishes, entertaining pieces
- [ ] Extra dish sets and glassware beyond daily use
- [ ] Cookbooks, recipe binders, table linens
- [ ] Wine, bar supplies, cocktail tools (wrap bottles individually, pack upright)
- [ ] Vases, countertop decor, decorative bowls
- [ ] Rarely used utensils and gadgets (mandoline, fondue set, spiralizer)
- [ ] Spices and pantry staples (check expiration dates first)
- [ ] KEEP OUT: one pot, one pan, one plate/bowl/mug per person, utensils, coffee maker, dish soap, paper towels, trash bags, snacks for the road
- [ ] LAST BOX (OPEN FIRST): paper plates, plastic utensils, dish soap, sponge, coffee setup, can opener, sharp knife, paper towels

**Declutter tip:** Duplicate whisks, three sets of measuring cups, spices older than 3 years, chipped dishes, and lidless containers all go. If you used it once in 2019, it's not coming to Oregon.

---

# LIVING ROOM

**Who:** J | **Time:** 3–4 hrs | **Priority:** Pack 2–3 wks out, keep one entertainment setup until the final days
**Boxes:** 4–8 medium, 2–3 small, 1–2 large, TV box or mirror box if needed

- [ ] Books (small boxes only, spine-down, never fill a large box with books)
- [ ] DVDs, games, vinyl records (upright like files, small boxes)
- [ ] TV (original box or moving blanket plus TV box, photograph cables first, remote in labeled zip-lock)
- [ ] Sound system, speakers, streaming devices, gaming consoles (wrap each, label all cords)
- [ ] Picture frames, art, mirrors (painter's tape X on glass, bubble wrap, FRAGILE)
- [ ] Lamps (remove shade, bag shade upright, wrap base separately)
- [ ] Throw pillows, blankets, curtains (use as padding or stuff in labeled trash bags)
- [ ] Rugs (roll tight, secure with twine or stretch wrap)
- [ ] Shelving and small furniture (disassemble, bag hardware, tape bag to furniture)
- [ ] Decorative items, candles, figurines, coasters
- [ ] All remotes and batteries into one labeled zip-lock bag

**Declutter tip:** Books are the heaviest things per cubic foot. If you won't reread it, donate it. Same for DVDs in a streaming era. Dead remotes, old magazines, and obligation decor all stay behind.

---

# PRIMARY BEDROOM

**Who:** P | **Time:** 2–3 hrs | **Priority:** Non-essentials 2–3 wks out, daily clothes and bedding morning of move
**Boxes:** 4–8 medium, 1–2 wardrobe boxes, 2–3 large

- [ ] Off-season clothing and shoes (wrap shoes in packing paper)
- [ ] Extra bedding sets, quilts, decorative pillows
- [ ] Jewelry (valuable pieces go in the car, not the truck — use a zip-lock or jewelry roll)
- [ ] Dresser contents (pack into labeled bags by drawer, or leave in drawers if movers allow)
- [ ] Nightstand contents: books, journals, chargers, personal items
- [ ] Under-bed storage items
- [ ] Wall art, mirrors, photos (see fragile rules)
- [ ] Hamper, iron, ironing board, extra hangers (bundle hangers with rubber bands)
- [ ] KEEP OUT: 3 days of clothes and underwear per person, pajamas, daily shoes, one sheet set, pillowcases, pillows (carry in car), phone charger
- [ ] LAST BOX (OPEN FIRST): sheets, pillowcases, phone chargers, hangers, bedside essentials

**Declutter tip:** Try everything on. Doesn't fit, don't love it, haven't worn it in a year — donate. Worn-out socks and underwear get tossed. Old pillows aren't worth shipping 2,400 miles.

---

# GUEST ROOM / SPARE ROOM

**Who:** M | **Time:** 1–2 hrs | **Priority:** Pack first — 4+ wks out
**Boxes:** 2–5 medium, 1 large

- [ ] Guest bedding and pillows
- [ ] Extra towels stored here
- [ ] Hobby and craft supplies
- [ ] Exercise equipment (disassemble if needed, wipe down)
- [ ] Stored luggage (use suitcases as packing containers for soft items)
- [ ] Board games, puzzles, card games
- [ ] Gift wrapping supplies
- [ ] Seasonal and holiday decorations
- [ ] Closet contents that have been untouched since the last move
- [ ] Miscellaneous storage bins and overflow items

**Declutter tip:** This room is the declutter gold mine. If you stored it here because you didn't know where else to put it, you probably don't need it in Oregon. Broken equipment, dusty craft projects you'll never finish, and guest bedding for a guest room you might not have are all fair game.

---

# BATHROOM(S)

**Who:** P | **Time:** 1–2 hrs per bathroom | **Priority:** Non-essentials 2 wks out, daily toiletries morning of move
**Boxes:** 1–3 small, 1 medium per bathroom

- [ ] Extra towels and washcloths beyond one per person
- [ ] Backup toiletries and bulk supplies
- [ ] Hair tools (straightener, curling iron, dryer — let cool, wrap cords)
- [ ] Medicine cabinet: first aid, bandages, cold medicine, vitamins (check all dates)
- [ ] Under-sink cleaning supplies (seal caps with plastic wrap, pack upright in lined box)
- [ ] Shower curtain (wash first or replace at destination), bath mat, wastebasket
- [ ] Rarely used items: nail kits, face masks, travel-size bottles
- [ ] KEEP OUT: toothbrushes, toothpaste, deodorant, soap, shampoo, contacts/glasses, daily meds, razor, one towel per person, 2 rolls toilet paper, hand soap
- [ ] LAST BOX (OPEN FIRST): toilet paper, hand soap, towels, toothbrushes, daily meds

**Declutter tip:** Check every expiration date. Hotel travel bottles, old makeup, dried nail polish, and that half-used product you didn't like all get tossed. Most people can cut bathroom items in half and never notice.

---

# HOME OFFICE / DESK AREA

**Who:** M | **Time:** 2–3 hrs | **Priority:** Non-essentials 2–3 wks out, keep work computer running until last possible day
**Boxes:** 3–5 medium, 2 small

- [ ] Books and reference materials
- [ ] File cabinet contents (sort, shred what you don't need, keep 2–3 yrs of tax records)
- [ ] Office supplies: staplers, tape, pens, paper
- [ ] Printers, scanners, shredders (original boxes if available, cords in labeled bags)
- [ ] Extra cables, adapters, chargers (label every one with what it connects to)
- [ ] Desk accessories and decor
- [ ] KEEP OUT: laptop and charger, external hard drives, USB backups, webcam, headset, notepad and pen
- [ ] ALL ELECTRONICS AND BACKUPS RIDE IN THE CAR, NOT THE TRUCK

**Declutter tip:** Shred old bank statements, expired warranties, and manuals (most are online). The drawer of phone cases for phones you don't own, ancient chargers, and broken headphones goes to e-waste recycling, not Oregon.

---

# GARAGE / STORAGE / UTILITY AREAS

**Who:** J | **Time:** 3–5 hrs | **Priority:** Pack first — 4+ wks out
**Boxes:** 3–10 medium plus loose items, original packaging for power tools

- [ ] Tools (consolidate into toolbox, wrap sharp edges in cardboard and tape)
- [ ] Garden tools and outdoor power equipment (clean soil off, drain all fuel — movers won't transport it)
- [ ] Holiday and seasonal decorations
- [ ] Sporting equipment: bikes, skis, camping gear
- [ ] Automotive supplies (drain or dispose of all fluids — oil, paint, gas, propane, pesticides are prohibited)
- [ ] Luggage and storage bins (use as packing containers)
- [ ] Paint cans (photograph labels for color matching, then leave behind or dispose)
- [ ] Ladders, shelving units (disassemble, bag hardware)
- [ ] Laundry supplies stored here
- [ ] Firewood: leave it — transporting firewood across state lines can spread invasive insects and may be restricted

**Declutter tip:** This is where things go to be moved from house to house forever. Broken items waiting to be fixed, duplicate tools, old paint, and mystery hardware — if you haven't touched it in 2 years, let it go. Dispose of hazardous materials at a local collection event.

---

# DINING ROOM

**Who:** P | **Time:** 1–2 hrs | **Priority:** Pack 2–3 wks out
**Boxes:** 2–5 medium, 1–2 small for heavy china

- [ ] China, fine glassware, crystal (wrap individually, pack on edge, fill all gaps, mark FRAGILE)
- [ ] Serving dishes, platters, centerpieces
- [ ] Table linens and cloth napkins
- [ ] Candlesticks and candles
- [ ] Buffet or hutch contents (pack contents, then disassemble furniture if needed)
- [ ] Chair cushions (into large trash bags labeled NOT TRASH)
- [ ] Dining table hardware (if it disassembles, bag hardware in zip-lock taped to underside)
- [ ] Wall art or mirrors in the dining area
- [ ] Bar cart contents if kept here

**Declutter tip:** Inherited formal sets you never use are heavy and expensive to move. If you display them out of obligation rather than love, this is the moment to pass them to a family member or consign them.

---

# LAUNDRY AREA

**Who:** P | **Time:** 30–60 min | **Priority:** Pack 1 wk out except for one final load
**Boxes:** 1–2 medium, 1 small

- [ ] Detergent, fabric softener, stain remover (seal caps with plastic wrap, zip-lock, pack upright)
- [ ] Dryer sheets, clothespins, lint roller
- [ ] Iron and ironing board (cool iron, wrap cord, collapse board, wrap in blanket)
- [ ] Drying rack (collapse and bundle with twine)
- [ ] Laundry baskets and hampers (use as packing containers for towels and rags)
- [ ] Spare hangers (bundle with rubber bands, bag and label NOT TRASH)
- [ ] Sewing kit, stain sticks, mending supplies
- [ ] Cleaning rags and microfiber cloths (keep 2–3 out for move-day cleaning)
- [ ] Washer and dryer if you own them (disconnect hoses, drain, secure drum with transit bolts — check your model's manual)

**Declutter tip:** Bottles less than a quarter full aren't worth sealing, packing, and shipping. Use them up or give them to a neighbor. Stained rags, single socks, and broken hangers get tossed.

---

# ENTRYWAY / MUDROOM / COAT CLOSET

**Who:** M | **Time:** 30–60 min | **Priority:** Pack 1–2 wks out except daily coats and shoes
**Boxes:** 1–2 medium, 1 large

- [ ] Off-season coats, jackets, hats, scarves, gloves
- [ ] Umbrellas
- [ ] Shoe rack and shoes beyond daily wear (wrap each pair in packing paper)
- [ ] Backpacks, tote bags, reusable shopping bags (stuff with soft items to save space)
- [ ] Pet leashes, harnesses, accessories stored here (keep one set out for travel)
- [ ] Spare keys (collect, label, decide what to return and keep)
- [ ] Mail organizer, entryway tray, miscellaneous drawer contents
- [ ] Welcome mat (shake out, roll, secure with twine)
- [ ] Wall hooks, mirror, entryway decor

**Declutter tip:** Count your reusable bags — you probably have thirty, keep five. Shoes that hurt, single gloves, broken umbrellas, and junk-drawer mystery keys all stay behind.

---

# OUTDOOR / PATIO

**Who:** J | **Time:** 1–2 hrs | **Priority:** Pack 2–3 wks out, clean and dry everything before boxing
**Boxes:** 1–3 medium plus loose furniture items

- [ ] Patio furniture (clean, dry, disassemble if possible, wrap legs and corners, bag hardware)
- [ ] Grill (clean thoroughly, remove and give away propane tank — movers won't transport it)
- [ ] Planters and pots (empty soil, clean, nest smaller inside larger with paper between)
- [ ] Garden hose (drain completely, coil, secure with twine)
- [ ] Outdoor cushions and pillows (into large trash bags labeled NOT TRASH)
- [ ] String lights, lanterns, outdoor decor
- [ ] Doormat (shake, roll, secure)
- [ ] Dog's outdoor toys
- [ ] Gardening gloves, hand tools, watering cans

**Declutter tip:** Cheap plastic patio furniture often costs less to replace than to ship. Cracked pots, rusted tools, and dead plants stay behind. Sell the grill and buy one in Oregon rather than paying to move it.

Glad it all came together. You've got a solid set of documents now — the master phased checklist, the 6-week calendar, the moving day one-pager, the room-by-room packing sheets, and the 10-week packing timeline.

When you're ready to act on it, I'd suggest printing the room sheets first and taping them to the door of each room. It makes the whole thing feel less overwhelming because you're only ever looking at one room's list at a time.

If anything comes up as you get into it — route planning, budget questions, what to do about specific items, Oregon-specific logistics — just come back and we'll figure it out.
